Documentation → Releases → 4.15.0

SATOM 4.15.0

Scout signs in to a model gateway through a connection, and connections work out their own session lifetime (SI-0013); one Software Update page for git and signed packages with Update methods; the Settings menu follows the section; event automations keep one open run per app and inputs; a standby that stays down is an alert; clearer discovery errors (SI-0007); vendor icon sets import in their own colours (SI-0012).

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
On this page
  • In short
  • Added
  • Changed
  • Removed
  • Fixed
  • After you upgrade

Released: 2026-11-24 · All releases

In short#

Everything in 4.14.1 and earlier applies. No database migration and no new Python dependencies. A server on 4.14.1, 4.14.0 or an earlier recent release can take the small delta package (satom-update-4.15.0-from-<your version>.tar.gz) instead of the full one.

Added#

  • Scout signs in to a model gateway whose token expires (SI-0013). A Scout provider (OpenAI-compatible) now has Sign in with: a Plugin Studio HTTP connection (Session login, OAuth2 client credentials or Bearer) instead of a fixed API key. SATOM signs in with the connection, renews the token by itself and, when the gateway answers 401, signs in again and retries once (a streamed answer too; never a loop). Test connection signs in the same way. See Scout and Connections.
  • Connections work out how long a session lives. Every Session login and OAuth2 connection has a Session lifetime field, Auto when empty: SATOM reads the lifetime from the login answer (expires_in, expires_at…), from the token itself (a JWT's exp) or from the session cookie's expiry, and renews a margin before the end. When nothing says it, the short default stays (4 minutes for Session login, 5 for OAuth2). A number typed there is a ceiling: when the server says the session ends sooner, the server wins. OAuth2 connections now also get a new token on a 401.

Changed#

  • One Software Update page for both ways of updating. The repository pane is now the Git repository section of Settings › Software Update, next to Signed packages and Update sources (moved from General). A new Update methods card picks Both (default), Git repository only or Signed packages only; the web, the CLI and the reconciler all obey it. With packages only, the primary's reconciler stops fetching; a standby always follows its primary. History rows name the method. Old links to /settings/#tab-git forward to the new section. See Software Update.
  • Settings: the menu follows you. Every group of the Admin Console menu is folded except the one holding the section on screen; sub-menus inside a group are expanded; the address bar carries the section, so a reload lands on the same place. Every card of a section is drawn open.

Removed#

  • "Pull now" on the repository pane. It pulled code without any of an update's steps. Check for updates → Apply does the same through the privileged runner. The manual git console stays, folded as advanced.

Fixed#

  • The reconciler no longer undoes a newer signed package. Updates now go by VERSION: a git update to an older version needs the downgrade confirmation, and the reconciler holds (held, naming both versions) instead of moving the node back.
  • Event automations: one open run per app and inputs. An automation that runs a Plugin Studio app ends skipped while a run of the same app with the same inputs is still running or waiting for a person, and a full run cap means wait (up to 3 minutes), not fail. See Triggers.
  • A standby that stays down is an alert. After 10 minutes without the HA standby (or its reconciler reporting), the alert engine raises No HA standby (critical). See Alerting.
  • Discovery errors say where, why and what to do (SI-0007). Endpoint errors are grouped by kind (appliance failed while answering, refused by the admin profile, licence, other FortiWeb error, no answer in time), each with its cause, what to do and every endpoint with its URN. See Rediscovery.
  • Diagram Studio: vendor icon sets import as downloaded, in their own colours (SI-0012). Stylesheet colours in SVG icons are now kept (same whitelist as attributes), white-only "reverse" twins are skipped, a library holds up to 1000 symbols, and a pack with its own colours is stored as a Colour library. Fortinet's library imports straight from its ZIP: https://icons.fortinet.com/Fortinet-Icon-Library.zip. SATOM ships no vendor artwork.

After you upgrade#

If you update only one way, choose it in Settings › Software Update › Update methods; until you do, both stay enabled as before.
